blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — toddler choking prevention
stem: Which instruction best reduces choking risk when feeding a toddler?

options.A: Prepare foods in developmentally appropriate shapes, sizes, and textures; have the child sit while eating; and supervise closely throughout the meal.
options.B: Offer whole grapes and round hot-dog pieces once the child chews table foods well, while maintaining close supervision during the meal.
options.C: Allow eating while walking or playing when the food is soft, because movement does not meaningfully change choking risk in toddlers.
options.D: Use whole nuts or hard candy as supervised snacks to strengthen chewing skills, provided an adult remains within arm's reach of the child.

rationale: A is correct. Current CDC choking-prevention guidance recommends preparing foods in the right shape, size, and texture for the child's development, having the child sit while eating, and watching the child at all times. CDC lists uncut grapes, hot dogs/sausages, whole or chopped nuts, and hard candy among potential choking hazards. B and D retain known choking hazards despite supervision. C conflicts with CDC guidance to have children sit while eating rather than walk or crawl.
educational_objective: Teach caregivers to reduce toddler choking risk through developmentally appropriate food preparation, seated eating, avoidance of common hazards, and direct supervision.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Choking Hazards — Infant and Toddler Nutrition; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC page dated March 11, 2026 and live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC Choking Hazards lines 32-52: prepare food to the right shape/size/texture for development, avoid small/sticky/hard foods, have the child sit while eating, and watch the child at all times. Lines 58-90 list hazards including uncut grapes, nuts/seeds, hot dogs/sausages, and hard candy.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports developmentally appropriate food preparation, seated eating, continuous supervision, and avoidance of common round/hard choking hazards.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: protect clients from injury and educate clients/caregivers on safety concerns.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; the clinical key is supported by current CDC HTML.

option_audit.A: Correct; combines CDC-supported food preparation, seated eating, and supervision.
option_audit.B: Plausible supervision-focused response but retains two explicitly listed choking hazards.
option_audit.C: Plausible soft-food exception but conflicts with seated-eating guidance.
option_audit.D: Plausible developmental rationale but uses explicitly listed choking hazards.

cueing_audit.answer_length: All options are comparable in length and structure; the key is not uniquely signaled by detail.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor relies on simplistic always/never/only wording.
